1.translation: The Blessed Lord said: Once more, mighty-armed one, hear my highest word, which I will speak to you, who take joy in it, because I wish you well.
1.nuances: All six agree on the sense; they differ on paramaṃ vacaḥ (Sivananda and Adidevananda 'supreme word', Purohit 'supreme advice', Sankaranarayan 'best message') and on prīyamāṇāya, which Sivananda, Purohit and Sankaranarayan take as 'beloved/dear to Me', Gambirananda as 'who take delight in it', Adidevananda as 'who love Me', and Prabhupada expands into 'My dear friend' plus a gloss that this knowledge surpasses what came before.

2.translation: Neither the hosts of gods nor the great seers know where I come from, for in every way I am the origin of the gods and of the great seers.
2.nuances: Prabhavam is read as 'origin' by Sivananda, Purohit and Sankaranarayan, as 'majesty' by Gambirananda, 'power' by Adidevananda, and 'origin or opulences' by Prabhupada; Sankaranarayan alone takes ādi as 'the first among' rather than 'source of', and Prabhupada writes 'demigods' for devāḥ.

3.translation: Whoever knows me as unborn and without beginning, the great Lord of the worlds, is undeluded among mortals and is released from all sins.
3.nuances: The renderings are essentially unanimous; the only shading is in lokamaheśvaram ('great Lord of the worlds' for most, 'Absolute Lord of the universe' in Sankaranarayan, 'Supreme Lord of all the worlds' in Prabhupada) and Prabhupada's added 'he only'.

4.translation: Understanding, knowledge, freedom from confusion, patience, truth, restraint of the senses, calm of the mind, pleasure and pain, coming to be and passing away, fear and fearlessness too,
4.nuances: Dama and śama are glossed as 'self-restraint, calmness' (Sivananda, Purohit), 'control of the external/internal organs' (Gambirananda), or 'control of the senses, control of the mind' (Prabhupada, Sankaranarayan); bhava/abhāva are 'existence/non-existence' for Sivananda, 'birth/death' for most others, and 'exaltation/depression' for Adidevananda, while asammoha is 'steadiness' in Sankaranarayan and 'freedom from doubt and delusion' in Prabhupada.

5.translation: non-harming, evenness, contentment, austerity, giving, fame and disgrace: all these varied states of beings arise from me alone.
5.nuances: All agree the qualities originate in Kṛṣṇa; bhāvāḥ is rendered 'qualities' (Sivananda, Adidevananda, Prabhupada), 'characteristics' (Purohit) or 'dispositions' (Gambirananda, Sankaranarayan), and Prabhupada turns 'arise from' into 'are created by Me', while Purohit has 'failure' for ayaśaḥ.

6.translation: The seven great seers of old and the four, and likewise the Manus, sharing my nature, were born from my mind; from them descend these creatures in the world.
6.nuances: The grouping is disputed: Sivananda, Purohit and Prabhupada count 'the ancient four' as a separate group (Purohit names them as the Kumāras), whereas Gambirananda, Adidevananda and Sankaranarayan read 'the four Manus'; madbhāvāḥ is 'possessed of powers like Me' (Sivananda), 'thoughts fixed on Me' (Gambirananda), 'My mental disposition' (Adidevananda) or simply 'come from Me' (Prabhupada), and Prabhupada widens loka to 'the various planets'.

7.translation: One who truly knows this pervading glory and this creative power of mine is joined to me in unwavering yoga; of this there is no doubt.
7.nuances: Vibhūti and yoga are 'manifold manifestations and Yoga-power' (Sivananda), 'manifested glory and Creative Power' (Purohit), 'majesty and yoga' (Gambirananda), 'opulence and mystic power' (Prabhupada); the resulting avikampa yoga becomes 'perfect peace' in Purohit, 'Yoga of Bhakti' in Adidevananda and 'unalloyed devotional service' in Prabhupada.

8.translation: I am the source of everything; from me all things proceed. Knowing this, the wise, filled with loving feeling, worship me.
8.nuances: Bhāvasamanvitāḥ is 'endowed with meditation' (Sivananda), 'unchanging devotion' (Purohit), 'filled with fervour' (Gambirananda), 'with all devotion' (Adidevananda) or 'with all their hearts' (Prabhupada); Sankaranarayan uniquely casts the first line as the wise men's own quoted thought in the third person, and Prabhupada adds 'spiritual and material worlds'.

9.translation: With their thoughts on me, their life-breath given over to me, awakening one another and always speaking of me, they are content and they delight.
9.nuances: All read madgataprāṇāḥ as life or lives absorbed in or dedicated to Kṛṣṇa (Adidevananda keeps 'Pranas'); Purohit drops the clause 'speaking of Me', and Prabhupada recasts the subject as 'My pure devotees' whose lives are devoted 'to My service'.

10.translation: To those who are constantly disciplined and worship me with love I give that yoga of understanding by which they come to me.
10.nuances: Buddhiyoga is 'Yoga of discrimination' (Sivananda), 'power of discrimination' (Purohit), 'possession of wisdom' (Gambirananda), 'mental disposition' (Adidevananda), 'knowledge-Yoga' (Sankaranarayan) and plain 'understanding' (Prabhupada); satatayuktānām is 'ever steadfast', 'always devout', 'ceaselessly united' or, in Prabhupada, 'constantly devoted to serving Me'.

11.translation: Out of compassion for them alone, I, dwelling in their own being, destroy the darkness born of ignorance with the shining lamp of knowledge.
11.nuances: Ātmabhāvasthaḥ divides them: 'dwelling within their Self' (Sivananda, Sankaranarayan), 'in their hearts' (Purohit, Gambirananda, Prabhupada), or Adidevananda's Viśiṣṭādvaita reading 'abiding in their mental activity as its object'; Purohit replaces 'compassion' with 'by My grace' and Prabhupada with 'special mercy'.

12.translation: Arjuna said: You are the supreme Brahman, the supreme abode, the supreme purifier; the eternal divine Person, the primal god, unborn and all-pervading,
12.nuances: Paraṃ dhāma is 'supreme abode' (Sivananda, Sankaranarayan, Prabhupada), 'Eternal Home' (Purohit) or 'supreme Light' (Gambirananda, Adidevananda); Gambirananda, Adidevananda and Sankaranarayan merge verses 12 and 13 and make 'eternal divine Person' the object of what the sages declare, while Prabhupada adds 'Absolute Truth' and 'all-pervading beauty'.

13.translation: so all the seers declare you, and so does the divine seer Nārada, and Asita, Devala and Vyāsa; and you yourself tell me so.
13.nuances: Sivananda, Purohit and Prabhupada render the verse on its own, with the seers confirming the previous verse's epithets; Gambirananda, Adidevananda and Sankaranarayan treat it as the continuation of 12, and Gambirananda notes that Nārada and the rest are named separately for their eminence.

14.translation: All this that you tell me I hold to be true, Keśava. Indeed, Blessed Lord, neither gods nor demons know your manifestation.
14.nuances: Vyakti is 'manifestation' (Sivananda, Purohit, Adidevananda, Sankaranarayan), 'glory' (Gambirananda) or 'personality' (Prabhupada); Sankaranarayan oddly reads dānavāḥ as 'great seers' where all others have 'demons' (Purohit: 'the godless').

15.translation: You alone know yourself by yourself, Supreme Person, source of beings, Lord of beings, god of gods, master of the world.
15.nuances: Only Prabhupada renders this verse in the source data, glossing ātmanā as 'by Your own internal potency' and bhūtabhāvana as 'origin of all'.

16.translation: You should tell me completely of your divine self-manifestations, those manifestations by which you abide, pervading these worlds.
16.nuances: Vibhūti is 'glories' (Sivananda), 'glorious manifestations' (Purohit), 'manifestations' (Gambirananda, Adidevananda), 'auspicious manifesting powers' (Sankaranarayan) or 'opulences' (Prabhupada); Sivananda and Sankaranarayan stress that Kṛṣṇa alone is capable of telling them, while Purohit and Prabhupada soften arhasi into 'please tell me'.

17.translation: How may I know you, Yogin, by meditating on you always? And in what particular forms, Blessed Lord, are you to be thought of by me?
17.nuances: The vocative yogin is kept by Sivananda, Gambirananda and Sankaranarayan, becomes 'Master' in Purohit and 'supreme mystic' in Prabhupada, and Adidevananda shifts it to Arjuna as 'Your devotee'; bhāveṣu is 'aspects or things', 'manifestations', 'objects', 'modes', 'entities' or 'forms'.

18.translation: Tell me again at length, Janārdana, of your power and your manifest glory, for hearing your nectar I am never sated.
18.nuances: Amṛtam is read as Kṛṣṇa's nectar-like words by all; yoga and vibhūti are 'Yogic power and glory' (Sivananda), 'power and glory' (Purohit), 'attributes and glories' (Adidevananda) and 'mystic power of Your opulences' (Prabhupada), and Gambirananda notes that 'again' refers back to chapters 7 and 9.

19.translation: The Blessed Lord said: Very well, I shall tell you my divine self-manifestations, but only the principal ones, best of the Kurus, for there is no end to my extent.
19.nuances: All agree only the chief manifestations will be given; prādhānyataḥ is 'in their prominence', 'chief aspects', 'according to their importance' or 'only the chief', and Purohit alone renders kuruśreṣṭha as 'My beloved friend' rather than 'best of the Kurus' or 'Arjuna'.

20.translation: I am the Self, Guḍākeśa, seated in the heart of every being; I am the beginning, the middle and the very end of beings.
20.nuances: Ātmā is 'the Self' for most, 'the Soul' for Sankaranarayan and 'the Supersoul' for Prabhupada; Sankaranarayan translates the epithet as 'conqueror of sleep', Purohit replaces 'the middle' with 'the life'.

21.translation: Of the Ādityas I am Viṣṇu; of lights, the radiant sun; of the Maruts I am Marīci; among the stars I am the moon.
21.nuances: Purohit allegorises throughout ('creative Powers... the Creator', 'Whirlwind among winds', 'Moon among planets'), whereas the rest keep the proper names; Gambirananda supplies the lists of twelve Ādityas and forty-nine Maruts, and Sankaranarayan renders Ādityas as 'sons of Aditi'.

22.translation: Of the Vedas I am the Sāmaveda; of the gods I am Vāsava; of the senses I am the mind; and in beings I am consciousness.
22.nuances: Cetanā is 'intelligence' (Sivananda, Purohit, Gambirananda), 'consciousness' (Adidevananda), 'sentience' (Sankaranarayan) or 'living force' (Prabhupada); Purohit turns Vāsava into 'the Electric Force in the Powers of Nature', and Prabhupada says 'demigods'.

23.translation: Of the Rudras I am Śaṅkara; of the Yakṣas and Rākṣasas, the Lord of wealth; of the Vasus I am Fire; of mountain peaks I am Meru.
23.nuances: Purohit again abstracts the names ('Forces of Vitality', 'Mammon to the heathen and the godless', 'Energy in fire, earth, wind...'), Prabhupada substitutes 'Lord Śiva' and 'Kuvera', and Gambirananda footnotes the eleven Rudras and eight Vasus.

24.translation: Of household priests, Pārtha, know me as the chief, Bṛhaspati; of army commanders I am Skanda; of waters I am the ocean.
24.nuances: Purodhasām is 'household priests of kings' (Sivananda), 'priests of kings' (Gambirananda), 'family Priests' (Adidevananda), 'royal priests' (Sankaranarayan) or simply 'priests' (Purohit, Prabhupada); sarasām is 'lakes', 'waters', 'large expanses of water' or 'reservoirs', and Prabhupada names Skanda as Kārttikeya.

25.translation: Of the great seers I am Bhṛgu; of utterances I am the single syllable; of sacrifices I am the sacrifice of quiet repetition; of unmoving things, the Himālaya.
25.nuances: All identify ekam akṣaram as Om; japayajña is 'silent repetition' (Sivananda), 'silent prayer' (Purohit), 'muttering prayer' (Sankaranarayan) or 'chanting of the holy names' (Prabhupada), and Gambirananda explains japa is best because it involves no injury.

26.translation: Of all trees I am the aśvattha; of the divine seers, Nārada; of the Gandharvas, Citraratha; of the perfected ones, the sage Kapila.
26.nuances: Aśvattha is 'Peepul' (Sivananda, Gambirananda, Sankaranarayan), 'sacred Fig-tree' (Purohit) and, against the others, 'banyan tree' in Prabhupada; Purohit calls Gandharvas 'heavenly singers' and makes Kapila one of the 'sages' rather than the siddhas.

27.translation: Of horses know me as Uccaiḥśravas, born of the nectar; of lordly elephants, Airāvata; and of men, the king.
27.nuances: Purohit alone replaces Uccaiḥśravas with 'Pegasus' and Airāvata with 'the White one'; Prabhupada glosses amṛtodbhavam as 'produced during the churning of the ocean', and the rest keep the names, Gambirananda and Sankaranarayan noting they belong to Indra.

28.translation: Of weapons I am the thunderbolt; of cows I am the wish-fulfilling cow; I am Kandarpa the begetter; of serpents I am Vāsuki.
28.nuances: Prajanaḥ Kandarpaḥ is 'the progenitor, the god of love' (Sivananda, Gambirananda), 'the cause of progeny' (Adidevananda), 'Passion in those who procreate' (Purohit) or 'of causes for procreation I am Kandarpa' (Prabhupada); Purohit renders Vāsuki as 'the Cobra' and Prabhupada names the cow 'surabhi'.

29.translation: Of the Nāgas I am Ananta; of water-creatures I am Varuṇa; of the ancestors I am Aryaman; of those who restrain I am Yama.
29.nuances: Saṃyamatām is 'governors' (Sivananda), 'rulers' (Purohit), 'maintainers of law and order' (Gambirananda), 'subduers' (Adidevananda), 'controllers' (Sankaranarayan) or 'dispensers of law' (Prabhupada); Purohit abstracts all four names ('King-python', 'Aqueous Principle', 'Father of fathers', 'Death').

30.translation: Of the Daityas I am Prahlāda; of reckoners I am Time; of beasts I am the lion; and of birds I am Vainateya.
30.nuances: Kalayatām is 'reckoners' (Sivananda, Gambirananda, Adidevananda) or 'subduers' (Prabhupada), and kālaḥ is 'Death' for Adidevananda, 'the Eternal Present' for Purohit; Purohit turns Daityas into 'the heathen' and Garuḍa into 'the Eagle', and Sankaranarayan has no rendering.

31.translation: Of purifiers I am the wind; of weapon-bearers I am Rāma; of fish I am the makara; of flowing streams I am the Jāhnavī.
31.nuances: Pavatām is 'purifiers' for most, 'speeders' as an alternative in Sivananda and 'moving things' in Adidevananda; makara is 'shark' (Sivananda, Gambirananda, Prabhupada), 'Crocodile' (Purohit) or left as 'Makara' (Adidevananda), and Sankaranarayan's text is garbled, mixing in the Prahlāda clause of verse 30.

32.translation: Of creations I am the beginning, the end and the middle too, Arjuna; of knowledges I am knowledge of the Self; of those who debate I am reasoned argument.
32.nuances: Vādaḥ is 'logic' (Sivananda), 'Discussion' (Purohit), untranslated 'vada' (Gambirananda), 'fair reasoning' (Adidevananda), 'argument' (Sankaranarayan) or 'the conclusive truth' (Prabhupada); Adidevananda reads sargāṇām as 'creatures' and glosses adhyātmavidyā as covering both individual and Universal Self.

33.translation: Of letters I am the letter A, and of compounds the dvandva; I alone am imperishable Time; I am the Ordainer facing every way.
33.nuances: Dhātā is 'the dispenser of the fruits of actions' (Sivananda, Gambirananda, Sankaranarayan), 'Preserver' (Purohit), 'Creator' (Adidevananda) or, specifically, 'Brahmā' (Prabhupada); Purohit calls the dvandva 'the copulative' and Adidevananda 'the alphabet a'.

34.translation: I am death that carries all away, and the arising of all that is yet to be; among feminine things I am fame, fortune, speech, memory, intelligence, steadfastness and forbearance.
34.nuances: Nārīṇām is 'feminine qualities' (Sivananda, Gambirananda), 'women' (Adidevananda, Prabhupada) or 'the wives of men' (Sankaranarayan), and Purohit omits it altogether; udbhavaḥ bhaviṣyatām is 'prosperity of those to be prosperous' (Sivananda, Gambirananda) versus 'origin of all that shall be' (Purohit, Adidevananda, Prabhupada).

35.translation: Of the sāman chants I am the Bṛhatsāman; of metres I am the Gāyatrī; of months I am Mārgaśīrṣa; of seasons I am the flower-bearer.
35.nuances: All name the same items; kusumākara is 'the flowery season' (Sivananda), 'Spring' (Purohit, Gambirananda) or 'flower-bearing spring' (Prabhupada), Sankaranarayan reads sāmnām as 'modes of singing', and Purohit and Prabhupada add the calendar equivalent of Mārgaśīrṣa.

36.translation: I am the gambling of cheats; I am the splendour of the splendid; I am victory, I am resolve, I am the goodness of the good.
36.nuances: Sattvam sattvavatām is 'goodness of the good' (Sivananda), 'Purity of the pure' (Purohit), 'sattva quality' (Gambirananda), 'magnanimity' (Adidevananda), 'energy' (Sankaranarayan) or 'strength of the strong' (Prabhupada); vyavasāyaḥ is 'determination', 'effort', 'resolution' or Prabhupada's 'adventure'.

37.translation: Of the Vṛṣṇis I am Vāsudeva; of the Pāṇḍavas, Dhanañjaya; of the sages too I am Vyāsa; of poets I am the poet Uśanas.
37.nuances: Kavi is 'poet' (Sivananda), 'sage' (Purohit), 'omniscient' (Gambirananda), 'seer' (Adidevananda, Sankaranarayan) or 'great thinker' (Prabhupada); Purohit substitutes 'Shri Krishna' and 'Shukracharya' for the names, and Sankaranarayan reads Vāsudeva patronymically as 'the son of Vasudeva'.

38.translation: Of those who chastise I am the rod; of those who seek victory I am statecraft; of secrets I am silence; of the knowing I am knowledge.
38.nuances: Daṇḍa is 'sceptre' (Sivananda, Purohit), 'rod' (Gambirananda), 'principle of punishment' (Adidevananda) or 'punishment' (Sankaranarayan, Prabhupada); nīti is 'statesmanship', 'Strategy', 'righteous policy', 'political wisdom' or 'morality', and Prabhupada expands damayatām into 'means of suppressing lawlessness'.

39.translation: And whatever is the seed of all beings, that too am I, Arjuna; there is no being, moving or unmoving, that could exist without me.
39.nuances: The translators are in agreement that Kṛṣṇa is the seed of all and nothing exists apart from him, differing only in Prabhupada's 'generating seed' and 'existences'.

40.translation: There is no end to my divine manifestations, Parantapa; this account of my manifest glory I have given only by way of example.
40.nuances: Uddeśataḥ is 'a brief statement' (Sivananda), 'by way of illustration' (Purohit, Gambirananda, Sankaranarayan), 'in brief' (Adidevananda) or 'a mere indication' (Prabhupada); the epithet is 'destroyer of enemies', 'scorcher of foes' or 'mighty conqueror of enemies', with Sivananda, Purohit and Adidevananda just writing 'Arjuna' or dropping it.

41.translation: Whatever being has glory, splendour or might, understand that each of these has arisen from a mere portion of my radiance.
41.nuances: Tejas is 'splendour' (Sivananda, Purohit, Prabhupada), 'power' (Gambirananda, Adidevananda) or 'illuminant' (Sankaranarayan); the three attributes are divided slightly differently (Purohit expands to four: glorious, excellent, beautiful, mighty) and Gambirananda restricts sattvam to living beings.

42.translation: But what use is all this detailed knowledge to you, Arjuna? I stand supporting this entire universe with a single fragment of myself.
42.nuances: Viṣṭabhya is 'supporting' (Sivananda), 'sustain' (Purohit, Adidevananda), 'sustaining in a special way' (Gambirananda), 'pervading' (Sankaranarayan) or 'pervade and support' (Prabhupada); all agree the whole world rests on one fraction of Kṛṣṇa.

43.translation: Om, That, the Real. Thus ends the tenth chapter, called the Yoga of Divine Manifestations, in the glorious Bhagavad Gītā, the Upaniṣads, the knowledge of Brahman, the science of yoga, the dialogue between Śrī Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna.
